title: A copy can be given its own size
goal: A copy of a component can be made wider or taller on its own. Today the width and height boxes are greyed out on a copy, so the same nav bar cannot be 1200 wide on a desktop screen and 375 wide on a phone screen without breaking it away from the family it belongs to.
notes: Evidence: queue/manager/shots/2026-09-04-1543-starter-copy.png, a real window capture of a selected copy, shows X and Y typable and W 78 / H 36 greyed. The refusal is in the model, not the panel: GroupLayoutEditing.canSetGroupLayout and ownsContentRules both say no to isComponentInstance, and ComponentInstances.swift line ~439 does group.layout = main.group?.layout on every sync, so a stack copy's width and height come from the original every time. docs/design/ui-building.md, the 'Not in this slice' paragraph under 'a copy is not asked to decide what its original decides', names a per copy layout override as a real feature waiting on an override that survives the sync and a way to reset it. That machinery now exists: the colour knob landed on 2026-09-04 with per copy answers, saved colour links and unlink, in ComponentProperties.swift and ComponentColorKnob.swift. Keep the size override in the same shape so there is one story about what a copy owns. Padding is deliberately NOT in this slice: size is the one people hit daily. Flow maths is GroupFlow.swift; Bounds.of reads layout.usedWidth / usedHeight, so a per copy size has to reach it.
acceptance: Picking a copy leaves the width and height boxes live: you can type a number and you can drag the copy's handles, and a copy nobody has resized still reads and follows the original's size
A copy that has been resized keeps its size when the original changes: recolour the original, retype its wording or change its spacing and the wide copy stays wide

What is inside a resized copy lines up in the new size the same way the original would if it were that size, so a stretched nav bar spreads and a hugging button refuses to be squeezed under its contents
There is one plain way to put a copy back to the original's size, said in the same words the rest of the Component section uses, and one undo puts a resize back

Ships behind next-components. To see it: open Photonz Next, show the Library, drop the starter nav bar twice, pick the second one, type 1200 into W, then pick the original and change its colour, and watch the wide copy keep its width and take the new colour
Tests in PhotonzCore cover a resize surviving a sync, the reset, an original that hugs and an original with a size, written before any app code
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task

log.note: Adversarial review before building. Walked it as a first-time user: the W and H boxes are already there and already dead, so unlocking them is the whole gesture and there is nothing new to learn. Three things the task did not settle, decided here: (1) a copy needs a visible sign it has stopped following, so the reset rides an "Its own size" row in the Component section, the same shape "Its own look" already has, rather than two u-turn buttons crammed beside W and H in a 264pt dock; (2) the size is owned per axis, so a nav bar copy can own its width and still follow the original height; (3) the danger case is a copy sitting in a stack or on a screen that STRETCHES it, because the flow calls the same resize path a handle drag does: without a guard every stretched copy would silently and permanently gain a size of its own. Cut from the slice: a per-axis reset button, and any floor on how small a copy may go, since a copy at 40 wide should behave exactly as the original would at 40 wide.

Shape: GroupContent gains instanceSize (per axis, optional), written over the original layout by syncComponentInstances and by the frame-size line for a copy of a screen. Layer.resized gains placedByContainer so GroupFlow can place a copy without claiming the size for it. allowsFrameResize opens up for copies, which turns on both the eight handles and the W/H fields at once.

Built and green. GroupContent.instanceSize (per axis, optional, saved only by a copy that has one) is written over the original layout by syncComponentInstances through InstanceSizing, and over the frame box for a copy of a screen. LayerScaling.resizingCopy is the resize: it records the side that changed and lays the contents out for the new box. Layer.resized gained placedByContainer so GroupFlow and a container scaling its children can place a copy without claiming the size for it. allowsFrameResize opened up for copies, which turned on the handles and the W/H fields together and made LayerGeometryEditing.instanceSizeReason dead, so it went. 16 new tests in ComponentInstanceSizeTests, two old tests rewritten where they held the refusal; whole suite 3173 green.

Adversarial review of the BUILT thing, on the real app (Scripts/playtest/copy-own-size-walk.json, probe, Screen Recording granted). It found a real bug the tests had not: a widened copy kept its title where 320 put it. A copy is REBUILT from its original after every edit, so its contents always arrive laid out for the original box, and a group that arranges nothing does not re-place what it holds when it is given a size. Fixed with InstanceSizing.fitted, which places the contents from the original box into the copy box by the same rules a resize of the original follows; LayerScaling.placingContents was factored out of resizing so there is one implementation. A regression test now holds it. Verified in the app afterwards: handle drag 320x48 to 460x84, typed W 1200, Revert Size back to 320x48, typed W 375, original H to 72 leaves the copy 375x72, one undo leaves it 375x48.

Audit at queue/audits/2026-09-04-copy-own-size.json with two real window captures. Doc updated: new "A copy can be given its own size" section in docs/design/ui-building.md, and the older "Not in this slice" paragraph amended, since a per copy size is no longer not in it.

A copy takes a width and a height like any other layer and keeps them: GroupContent.instanceSize written over the original's layout by the sync (InstanceSizing), LayerScaling.resizingCopy for the resize, placedByContainer so a copy stretched by a stack claims nothing, and an Its own size row in the Component section that puts both sides back. Verified on the probe end to end (handle drag 320x48 to 460x84, typed 1200, revert, 375, original H 72 leaves the copy 375x72, one undo leaves it 375x48). 3173 tests green. Audit queue/audits/2026-09-04-copy-own-size.json with two real captures; follow-up filed for the Layout section's now half-wrong sentence.
